title: The HOTAIRM1-miR-222 Axis Regulates Resistance to Venetoclax and Defines a High Risk Subset in AML with t(8;21)(q22;q22.1); RUNX1::RUNX1T1
description: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with the RUNX1::RUNX1T1 fusion or t(8;21)(q22;q22.1) is a well-defined cytogenetic subtype. However, disease heterogeneity and therapy resistance suggest the involvement of additional molecular contributors beyond cytogenetic abnormalities. We investigated the role of the non-coding RNA axis HOTAIRM1-miR-222 in mediating venetoclax resistance and its prognostic significance in pediatric t(8;21) AML. Whole transcriptome sequencing revealed significant downregulation of the myeloid differentiation-associated long non-coding RNA HOTAIRM1 (P < 0.0001). This was independently validated using three datasets: (1) single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE116256), (2) the leukemia MILE study (GSE13159; AML n = 458), and (3) our internal study cohort (IRCH cohort; AML n = 106). Functional assays showed that HOTAIRM1 negatively regulates miR-222, an oncomiR consistently upregulated across AML cell lines (GSE1908 and current study), AML leukemic stem and progenitor cells (GSE117090), AML plasma-derived exosomes (GSE142699), patient samples from our internal cohort, and the TARGET AML dataset (AML n = 283 at baseline, n = 214 at relapse). We further identified miR-222 as a regulator of key genes involved in the cell cycle (p27/Kip1) and apoptosis pathways (BCL-2, BCL-xL, and MCL-1). Epigenetic restoration of HOTAIRM1 expression reduced miR-222 (P < 0.0001), inhibited the cell cycle, and promoted apoptosis in venetoclax-resistant Kasumi-1 cells. Machine learning-based feature selection (Random Forest, XGBoost) and Cox regression analysis consistently linked high miR-222 expression with poor outcomes in pediatric t(8;21) AML. This association was validated across both our internal and an external multi-institutional cohort, namely the TARGET AML dataset. These findings support the integration of miR-222 expression into current risk stratification systems to improve identification of high-risk patients within the conventionally favorable t(8;21) AML subgroup.
